$comment: Single source of truth for Loom label semantics (#10013). Embedded in loom-daemon; the Loom block of .github/labels.yml and defaults/.github/labels.yml is GENERATED from this file by `loom-daemon labels generate`. Edit here, then run `loom-daemon labels generate --write`.

stale_after_minutes is LIVE for the five claim labels (#11898): it is the default claim-liveness window, read by claim reconciliation and loom-daemon's claim_liveness module, and pinned by test to the shell defaults (claim-staleness.sh, check-evaluating-staleness.sh) and, for loom:building, to the lease TTL (Builder liveness is the renewed lease). Env overrides (LOOM_STALE_<NAME>_MINUTES, LOOM_LEASE_TTL_MINUTES) still win. lifecycle is INERT: no consumer reads it yet. contradicts_approval is the 1-based report order of labels that contradict loom:pr (null = does not contradict).

retired lists labels Loom no longer declares, with their old -> new mapping (#11513), consumed by the forge-side migration (#11511). It is NEVER rendered into labels.yml (sync-labels.sh is additive and would re-create it). replaced_by names an active label or null (remove, no replacement); owned=false means Loom never declared the label, so the migration only adds replaced_by and never removes or deletes it. also_remove (optional, owned only) lists active labels the migration also strips from each relabelled item, for a label that meant a combination (#11860).
yaml_header: # LOOM-MANAGED BLOCK — everything between the BEGIN/END LOOM LABELS markers is
# owned by Loom and is refreshed wholesale on every install/upgrade; edits made
# in here WILL be lost. To add your repo's own labels, put them OUTSIDE this
# block (above the BEGIN marker or below the END marker) — the installer and
# uninstaller only ever touch the marked range, so your labels are preserved
# across install, upgrade, and uninstall. See #4187.
# These labels coordinate the Loom AI agent workflow
# Sync with: .loom/scripts/sync-labels.sh (from the installed repo root)
# Or manually: gh label create/edit commands
#   THIS FILE IS GENERATED from defaults/labels.json (the label registry, the
#   single source of truth for label semantics). Do NOT edit it by hand: edit
#   defaults/.github/labels.yml (the installer template copied into fresh
#   installs) are both generated and therefore BYTE-IDENTICAL. CI enforces it
#   label_registry unit tests — the build fails on any drift.

yaml_preamble: # Core Workflow States

labels.name: loom:issue
labels.description: Approved for work. Applied by: humans, Champion, sweep gate — see curator.md.

labels.name: loom:building
labels.description: Builder is implementing this issue. Applied by: Builder only (claim label).
yaml_preamble: # Role-specific claim labels (they replaced one shared in-progress label):
# - loom:building (Builder implementing issue)
# - loom:curating (Curator enhancing issue)
# - loom:reviewing (Judge reviewing PR)
# - loom:treating (Doctor fixing bug/PR feedback)
# PR verdict-label mutual exclusion (#4570): {loom:review-requested,
# loom:reviewing, loom:changes-requested, loom:pr} form a mutually-exclusive
# verdict class on a PR — at most ONE of these four should be present at a
# time, with one legal transient exception: `loom:review-requested` and
# `loom:reviewing` may coexist while a Judge's claim is active (the review is
# in progress but has not yet produced a verdict). `loom:changes-requested`
# and `loom:pr` are terminal verdicts and must never coexist with each other,
# nor with a live `loom:reviewing` claim from a DIFFERENT actor's concurrent
# review. A PR observed carrying `loom:pr` + `loom:changes-requested` (or,
# equally invalid, `loom:pr` + `loom:review-requested` — twelve open PRs were
# found in this state on 2026-08-28, #7018) simultaneously is in an off-graph,
# contradictory state (see the PR #4560 incident, 2026-07-30) that must never
# be auto-merged — Champion's Verdict-State Janitor
# (defaults/.claude/commands/loom/champion-pr-merge.md) resolves it fail-safe
# (`loom:pr` always loses; whichever OTHER label is present wins), and
# Judge/Doctor's Verdict-Time CAS Recheck (judge.md / doctor.md) is the
# write-time guard that prevents it from being produced in the first place.
# `verdict-staleness-guard.sh` and `loom-daemon`'s `reconcile_pr_verdicts`
# both strip EVERY terminal verdict label on a stale-verdict clear, not just
# the one they detected as stale, so a stray copy of the other cannot survive
# that transition either (#7018).
# PR verdict labels are SHA-scoped (#5686): `loom:changes-requested` and
# `loom:pr` are statements about the specific tree they were rendered against,
# not about the PR as an object. Judge stamps every verdict comment with
# `<!-- loom:verdict-sha sha=<head-sha> verdict=approved|changes-requested -->`,
# and once the PR's head SHA moves (rebase, force-push, or new commits) that
# verdict is STALE: it is cleared and the PR returns to `loom:review-requested`
# for a fresh evaluation. Enforced by defaults/scripts/verdict-staleness-guard.sh
# (called from judge.md's Stale-Verdict Sweep, doctor.md's Stale-Verdict Check,
# and champion-pr-merge.md's Verdict-State Janitor Part 2) with an always-on
# daemon backstop in loom-daemon's claim_reconciliation `reconcile_pr_verdicts`
# pass. A stale APPROVAL is the dangerous direction — before #5686 it let
# Champion auto-merge a tree no Judge had reviewed. A verdict carrying no marker
# at all (written before this convention) fails safe: it is kept, never
# force-cleared.
# Role-Specific Workflow Labels

labels.name: loom:curating
labels.description: Curator is enhancing this issue. Applied by: Curator only (claim label).

labels.name: loom:treating
labels.description: Doctor is fixing this bug or PR. Applied by: Doctor. Stale after LOOM_STALE_TREATING_MINUTES (60m).

labels.name: loom:reviewing
labels.description: Judge is reviewing this PR. Applied by: Judge only. Stale after LOOM_STALE_REVIEWING_MINUTES (30m).

labels.name: loom:evaluating
labels.description: Champion is evaluating this proposal (claim label, stale after 15m). Applied by: Champion only.

labels.name: loom:review-requested
labels.description: PR ready for Judge to review. Applied by: Builder when opening PR.

labels.name: loom:changes-requested
labels.description: PR requires changes before re-review (Judge requested modifications). Applied by: Judge.

labels.name: loom:merge-conflict
labels.description: PR has merge conflicts requiring resolution

labels.name: loom:sequenced
labels.description: Approved, but sequenced behind another PR. Applied by: the sequencing pass or an operator.
labels.applied_by: the sequencing pass or an operator
labels.color_note: yellow-700 - a scheduling hold, one shade apart from the in-progress ambers and the operator orange
yaml_preamble: # loom:sequenced (#9378) is the durable "approved, but not yet" ordering hold:
# NOT an escalation (loom:operator means a human must rule; a landing order
# does not) and NOT loom:blocked (an issue-status label that is not a merge
# gate). The label is refused by merge-pr.sh's verdict-contradiction guard
# beside loom:pr, with the same no-override treatment. The condition it waits
# on lives in a trusted `<!-- loom:sequence after=… pred_head=… follower_head=…
# plan=… -->` marker on the PR, evaluated by `loom-daemon merge-pr
# sequence-eval`; clearing is REMOVING THE LABEL once the recorded predecessor
# has landed at the recorded head — a mechanical condition, never a memory.

labels.name: loom:auto-merge-ok
labels.description: Override a Champion merge-risk hold (applied by Judge or human)

labels.name: loom:ci-failure
labels.description: PR has failing CI checks

labels.name: loom:pr
labels.description: PR approved by Judge, ready for Champion auto-merge. Applied by: Judge.

labels.name: loom:blocked
labels.description: Waiting on something named (another change, a capability); released once it resolves
yaml_preamble: # Status Labels
# loom:blocked: waiting on something named, released when it resolves. Applied
# with `loom-daemon park-record apply` (a park record in the body). Two shapes
# need no other change to clear (#11861): a capability-only park (a
# <!-- loom:capability=<name> --> marker, no named blocker, no decision block),
# which a host holding that capability may attempt in propose-only mode
# (#6893); and Champion's merge-risk / critical-file PR hold, the ONE shape in
# which loom:pr may coexist with loom:blocked (a reason-only park record plus
# Champion's hold-state marker comment). Champion re-evaluates and releases
# that hold; merge-pr.sh still refuses to merge while it stands.

labels.name: loom:blocked-unnamed
labels.description: loom:blocked names no blocker: queued for Curator to name it or release it
labels.removed_by: Curator (after naming the blocker, recording a reason, or releasing the block) or the daemon tick once the issue is documented
yaml_preamble: # loom:blocked-unnamed (#10558): a queue marker, NOT a park label. It coexists
# with loom:blocked. Applied by the daemon tick to an open loom:blocked issue
# that names no blocker and states no reason; removed by Curator after it names
# the blocker, records a reason, or releases the block.

labels.name: loom:abort
labels.description: Signal to abort the sweep for this issue (returns to loom:issue)

labels.name: loom:decision-malformed
labels.description: Decision bounced for a missing/invalid decision block; Curator repairs or re-routes (#10057)

labels.name: loom:operator
labels.description: A human must act or decide; the body's decision block says what. Only a human removes it.
labels.applied_by: any role escalating to a human (operator-decision apply for decisions); merge-pr.sh #8508 escalation
yaml_preamble: # Holds (#11795): three labels, one meaning each. loom:blocked = waiting on
# something named (another change, a capability), released automatically;
# loom:operator = a human must act or decide now; loom:frozen = not now.
# loom:operator is the "a human is needed" state (#5502). It is a no-op for
# every role (#11861): a park on issues AND pull requests, so no dispatch
# route and no Curator, Champion, Judge, Doctor or Builder step acts on it
# until a human removes the label. What the human must do comes from the
# body, not a sub-label: a ```decision block (#10057) makes it a decision. It
# folds the retired loom:operator-only, -decision, -mechanical and -blocked
# labels (a named blocker stays in the body text).
# Applied by any role escalating to a human, by `loom-daemon operator-decision
# apply`, by merge-pr.sh's #8508 escalation
# (defaults/docs/merge-pr-exit-code-exceptions.md) and by its
# partial-increment reset (#9264) when the issue body carries a
# `loom:remainder-hold` marker. Removed by a human. Champion's merge-risk and
# critical-file PR holds are loom:blocked, not this label (#11861).

labels.name: loom:frozen
labels.description: Not now, don't touch: no agent or daemon path acts on it. Humans apply and remove it.
labels.color_note: slate-400 - inert, not an action signal
yaml_preamble: # loom:frozen (#11743) means "not now, don't touch": nothing is pending, so
# nothing re-evaluates it. Unlike loom:blocked (waiting on something, released
# automatically) no agent or daemon path reads it as work, comments on it,
# relabels it or dispatches it. A human applies it and only a human removes it.
# It is a park, a skip and a hard exclusion (hard-exclusion-labels.sh).

labels.name: loom:important
labels.description: Priority 2 of 3: taken before unlabeled work, not a hold. Applied by: operator, Guide, Champion.
yaml_preamble: # loom:important (#11103) is the middle of Loom's three priority levels (none /
# important / very important). Within a workspace the queue order is level,
# then oldest createdAt, then issue number. NOT a hold, never inherited by the
# daemon: whoever sets the priority labels a blocker too. Applied by / removed
# by: the operator, Guide and Champion alike.

labels.name: loom:very-important
labels.description: Priority level 3 of 3: wins the workspace draw. Capped at 1 per workspace; extras rank important.
yaml_preamble: # loom:very-important (#11103) is the top priority level. A workspace holding
# dispatchable very-important work wins the workspace draw. Capped at one per
# workspace (#11509): only the oldest open one counts, the rest rank as
# loom:important, enforced at dispatch (see priority-model.md). NOT a hold,
# never inherited by the daemon. Applied by / removed by: the operator, Guide
# and Champion alike.

yaml_preamble: # External Contribution Gate
# Not part of the loom: workflow. A non-collaborator submission needs maintainer
# approval before Curator/Builder process it.
# This is a HARD EXCLUSION (#7528): no Loom role may curate, build, or promote
# it, AND loom-daemon's work finder will not dispatch a sweep for it. The
# authoritative list lives in ONE place — `defaults/scripts/hard-exclusion-labels.sh`
# (mirrored by `loom_daemon::hard_exclusion::HARD_EXCLUSION_LABELS`, kept in
# lockstep by a unit test). Adding a hard exclusion means editing that list, not
# just adding a label here.
